technical_and_design_decisions: U1 and U7 share the JDBC to HDFS theme; they will be treated as two separate deliverables to avoid hidden coupling between user stories.
U4 and U5 (Storm / Spark Streaming comparison) are produced as standalone Markdown documents within the samples repository rather than as runnable code, since they are explicitly comparison-oriented.
U3 is treated as a build-system refactor: documentation generation will be migrated to a standard Gradle/Sphinx or Asciidoctor pipeline and the legacy pushGeneratedDocs task will be removed.

U8 requires a small, additive change to the file-sink module: a new --nameExpression stream-definition option that, when set, takes precedence over the existing filename-generator-expression attribute. No breaking change to existing behavior is introduced.
U2 (Sqoop) samples will follow the existing Spring XD batch job conventions (Spring Batch + XD batch module), keeping consistency with other samples in the repo.

U6 (Smart Grid demo port) assumes the s1-2014 source is available either in an internal repository or recoverable from prior commits; it will be re-targeted to the current Spring XD runtime and re-tested.
assumptions: The developer is a single, experienced Java/Spring engineer (no ramp-up time included).
A 1 workday = 8 hours of focused, uninterrupted development effort (not elapsed calendar duration).
The Spring XD runtime, Kafka, Sqoop, Storm, and Spark Streaming environments are already available and not provisioned as part of this increment.
Existing Spring XD modules (file sink, batch module, stream module) are stable and can be extended without re-architecting.
Smart Grid demo source (s1-2014) is accessible; if not, effort may increase but is not double-counted here.
No production-grade hardening, performance tuning, or full multi-tenant testing is required; samples are demonstration-grade.
Documentation is written in Asciidoctor/Markdown to match the existing samples repo convention.
U1 covers one cohesive Kafka-based sample application demonstrating the listed sub-use cases rather than four completely separate pipelines.
U2 delivers one batch job covering both JDBC→HDFS and HDFS→JDBC directions in a single project, exercised via two job configurations.

activities.activity_description: Review all eight user stories, clarify scope, identify shared building blocks (e.g., JDBC to HDFS overlap between U2 and U7), sketch the file-sink nameExpression contract, and produce a short design note covering the Kafka, Sqoop, and Smart Grid samples.

Implement a Spring XD data pipeline sample using Kafka as the message bus. Cover log aggregation and analysis, lambda architecture (code deduplication, decoupling of business logic), and reliable reprocessing. Provide stream/batch definitions, source code, and sample input data.
Create a Spring XD batch sample that uses Sqoop to move data JDBC to HDFS and HDFS to JDBC. Include job configuration, source code, and a README explaining how to run the sample.
Update the Gradle build regarding documentation generation: remove the pushGeneratedDocs task and any no-longer-needed link rewriting logic. Verify the docs still build cleanly.
Produce a comparison document for Storm examples in Spring XD from a field-engineer/implementation perspective, including code-shape mapping, deployment differences, and trade-offs.

activities.activity_name: U5 - Spark Streaming examples comparison document
activities.activity_description: Produce a comparison document for Spark Streaming examples in Spring XD from a field-engineer/implementation perspective, including code-shape mapping, deployment differences, and trade-offs.

Port the Smart Grid demo from the s1-2014 codebase into the current Spring XD samples repository. Adapt module references, dependencies, and runtime configuration; verify it runs end-to-end on the current XD distribution.

activities.activity_name: U7 - JDBC to HDFS data movement example
activities.activity_description: Create a focused example demonstrating JDBC to HDFS data movement in Spring XD, using the XD batch module and a clear, minimal configuration so field engineers can run it standalone.

Extend the file-sink module to accept an alternative --nameExpression option on stream definitions, giving full control over the underlying filename-generator-expression. Add unit and integration tests, and update reference documentation.

Run the Kafka, Sqoop, Smart Grid, and JDBC-to-HDFS samples end-to-end on a local XD runtime; verify the new file-sink nameExpression behavior; smoke-test Storm and Spark Streaming comparison content against the current samples.

activities.activity_name: Final documentation polish and code review
activities.activity_description: Review all new READMEs, ensure Asciidoctor/Markdown renders correctly with the updated Gradle pipeline, fix broken links introduced by the U3 link-rewriting removal, and conduct a self code review pass.
